pages.text: ## Popular numbers we don't repeat, and why Some of the most widely quoted screen time figures don't hold up when you trace them to their source. We left them out. "People check their phones 96 (or 352) times a day" Both come from surveys sponsored by the tech-care company Asurion (2019 and 2022) that don't say how checks were counted. People can't reliably recall around 100 daily events, and a near-fourfold jump in three years across different survey firms isn't plausible. The best measured figure is 51 pickups a day, for teens. "Americans check their phones 144 (or 186) times a day" [...] ### How much screen time is too much for adults? There is no official limit for adults. Research links long sessions and bedtime phone use with worse sleep, and trials show that cutting social media or phone time by 30 to 60 minutes a day can modestly improve well-being. ### How many times a day do people check their phones? The best measured figure is a median of 51 pickups a day for US teens (Common Sense Media, 2023). Widely shared adult figures such as 96 or 352 checks a day come from sponsored surveys that don't explain how checks were counted. ### How much time do French people spend on screens?

answerStatements.text: Asurion's November 2019 press release said Americans check their phones 96 times a day, about once every 10 minutes, based on its own research
Asurion described this as a 20 percent daily increase from a similar survey it conducted two years earlier

The figure comes from a single company's survey. The provided origin does not give enough detail to show how checks were counted, so it cannot establish that 96 is a verified measure of all Americans' behavior
